description: Demolition and re-development to provide a two storey dwelling (1 x 4 beds); parking; hard and soft landscaping; bin / cycle storage
decision_conditions:
<p>All planting, seeding or turfing included in the approved details of landscaping shall 
be carried out in the first planting season and first seeding season following the 
occupation of the building. Any trees or plants which within a period of 5 years from 
the occupation of the building die, are removed or become seriously damaged or 
diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size 
and species.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General 
Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re
enacting that order with or without modification), no development which would 
otherwise fall within Classes A, B, D, and E in Part 1 of Schedule 2 shall take 
place without the prior permission of the local planning authority.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General 
Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re
enacting that order with or without modification), no development within Schedule 
2, Part 3, Class L to that Order shall be carried out without the prior written 
permission of the local planning authority.&nbsp;</p>
The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

No site works or development shall commence until details of the levels of the 
building(s), road(s) and footpath(s) in relation to the adjoining land and highway(s), 
and any other changes proposed in the levels of the site, have been submitted to, 
and approved by, the local planning authority.

<p>Tree Plan</p><p>No site clearance, preparatory work or development shall commence until the 
detailed arboricultural information, including the final Arboricultural Method 
Statement, Arboricultural Impact Assessment, and Tree Protection Plan, has been 
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved 
tree protection measures shall be installed prior to the commencement of any 
works and shall be retained in situ for the duration of the construction period.&nbsp;</p>

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the 
following documents and plans, including full demolition of the existing 
dwellinghouse, prior to the commencement of the development:  
Fire Safety Statement, Design and Access Statement, Flood Risk Assessment, 
Heritage Statement, Arboricultural Report, Tree Protection Plan, Building Survey 
Report, Site Location Plan, PAGE. 01, PAGE. 01A, PAGE. 02, PAGE 03, PAGE. 
04, (Plans for South View Lodge)

<p>Prior to progression to damp proof course level, details of two built‑in bat boxes 
shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The 
details shall include the exact locations of the bat boxes and their full 
specification, clearly shown on the relevant elevation plans. The bat boxes shall 
be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of&nbsp;the development and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime 
of the development. </p>

<p>Evidence of certification of Secure by Design Accreditation for the development 
shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval in writing 
before any part of the development is occupied or used. The development shall 
only be completed and occupied in accordance with the approval.&nbsp;</p>

<p>The windows and doors in the first floor elevation of the proposed development 
facing towards Oak Lodge shall: (a) be of purpose-made obscure glass, (b) be 
permanently fixed closed below a height of 1.7m above finished floor level, and 
shall thereafter be retained in that form.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Construction Logistics Plan </p><p>No construction works shall take place, including demolition, until a Construction 
Method Statement and Logistics Plan has been submitted to, and approved in 
writing by, the local planning authority. It shall provide for:  
a)  
b)  
c)  
d)  
e)  
f)  
detailed timeline the  implementation of the development  
the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors;  
loading and unloading of plant and materials;  
storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development;  
measures to control the emission of dust and dirt during construction; and  
scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and 
construction works.  
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Method 
Statement &amp; Logistics Plan, or any amendment or variation to it as may be agreed 
in writing by the local planning authority throughout the construction period.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Landscaping</p><p>Notwithstanding the approved details, the development hereby permitted shall not 
proceed above the damp proof course level until a revised scheme of hard and 
soft landscape works for the whole site has been submitted to, and approved in 
writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Soft landscape works shall include: planting plans (at a scale not less than 1:100), 
schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes, plant container sizes (all at time 
of planting) and proposed numbers / densities.</p><p>Hard landscape works shall include; details of boundary treatments (materials, 
scale of boundary, location) and details of hard surfacing materials to be used in 
the landscaping of the site. The hard surfacing materials shall be permeable and 
details relating to the long-term maintenance and management of the on-site 
drainage shall be included. 
Written specification of planting and cultivation works to be submitted and 
landscape implementation programme with proposed timing / dates for the works.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Details of Materials </p><p>
Notwithstanding the approved plans, the construction of the replacement 
dwellinghouse hereby permitted shall not proceed above the damp proof course 
level until details of the materials to be used in the construction of the external 
surfaces of: 
(a) 
(b) 
the replacement dwelling (Brickwork type, brick bond, colour, texture and 
finish) 
Windows and doors (Detailed drawings at 1:20 or 1:50 scale showing 
window and door design, materials and colour finish)&nbsp;</p><p>The development shall be completed in accordance with the approved details 
and shall thereafter be retained.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Bat Box Provision </p><p>Notwithstanding the approved plans, the construction of the replacement 
dwellinghouse hereby permitted shall not proceed above the damp proof course 
level until details of the materials to be used in the construction of the external 
surfaces of: </p><p>a) the replacement dwelling (Brickwork type, brick bond, colour, texture and 
finish)</p><p>b)&nbsp;finish) 
Windows and doors (Detailed drawings at 1:20 or 1:50 scale showing 
window and door design, materials and colour finish)</p><p> </p><p>The development shall be completed in accordance with the approved details and 
shall thereafter be retained.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Self-Build </p><p>
Prior to the Occupation of the Development hereby permitted the Owner shall 
submit documents to the Local Planning Authority for approval confirming the 
dwelling meets the statutory definition of a self-build as set out in the Self-build 
and Custom Housebuilding Act 2015 defined as “self-build and custom 
housebuilding” means the building or completion by— (a)individuals, 
(b)associations of individuals, or (c)persons working with or for individuals or 
associations of individuals, of houses to be occupied as homes by those 
individuals 4&nbsp;</p>

<p>Fire Safety Statement</p><p> 
Notwithstanding the submitted details and approved plans, the development 
hereby permitted shall not progress beyond damp proof course level, until a Fire 
Safety Statement is submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning 
Authority, this statement shall include details of how the development will function 
in terms of the following: 
a)  
b)  
c)

f)  
identify suitably positioned unobstructed outside space:  
i)  
for fire appliances to be positioned on 
ii)  
appropriate for use as an evacuation assembly point 
is designed to incorporate appropriate features which reduce the risk to life 
and the risk of serious injury in the event of a fire; including appropriate fire 
alarm systems and passive and active fire safety measures 
is constructed in an appropriate way to minimise the risk of fire spread 
provide suitable and convenient means of escape, and associated 
evacuation strategy for all building users 
develop a robust management strategy for evacuation which is to be 
periodically updated and published (details of how often this management 
strategy is to be reviewed and published to be included), and which all 
building users can have confidence in 
provide suitable access and equipment for firefighting which is appropriate 
for the size and use of the development. The development shall be operated 
in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity. 
The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved details 
in perpetuity.&nbsp;</p>
